question: Which matrix factorization methods do they use?

extractive_spans: weighted factorization of a word-context co-occurrence matrix
evidence: Word embeddings that leverage subword information were first introduced by BIBREF14 which represented a word of as the sum of four-gram vectors obtained running an SVD of a four-gram to four-gram co-occurrence matrix. Our model differs by learning the subword vectors and resulting representation jointly as weighted factorization of a word-context co-occurrence matrix is performed.

title: Incorporating Subword Information into Matrix Factorization Word Embeddings
answer_rationale: The document explicitly states in section 'Subword LexVec' (Text 4) that the paper compares two types of subwords: simple n-grams (like fastText) and unsupervised morphemes. Additionally, section 'Materials' (Text 5) confirms that the models LV-N (n-grams) and LV-M (morphemes) are trained and evaluated. The conclusion (Text 7) also summarizes that subword information (n-grams and unsupervised morphemes) was incorporated into the LexVec model.
